subject: Intermittent streaming stalls during afternoon peak — mitigation checklist & follow-up

Can your team advise immediate mitigations we can do on our side and any temporary config changes on Redwood? This is impacting conversions.

Thanks Diane — and sorry you saw this during a peak. We're triaging now. Initial notes and short-term mitigations below.

Short-term actions you can take immediately (no code changes required):
- Switch to poll-based fetch for critical flows: replace streaming endpoint with a 1s poll loop to reduce client head-of-line impact.
- Reduce max_concurrent_streams per client to 3 in your front-end config (we can give you a toggle).
- Enable conservative client-side retry: 1 retry with exponential backoff starting at 300ms to avoid synchronized retries.

Immediate actions we're taking (Redwood ops):
- Spinning up extra edge workers in us-west-2 to relieve shard hot spots (active).
- Temporarily widen batching thresholds for FastShop sessions so smaller requests don't queue behind very large ones.
- Enabling a per-tenant routing override so your traffic bypasses the overloaded edge shard.

Can you confirm whether you can flip the max_concurrent_streams toggle? If not, we'll apply the routing override first.

I'll keep this thread updated.

Mina Haddad

Temporary config we pushed (can be reverted once stable):

- batch_size_soft_limit: increased by 25% to reduce head-of-line waits for interactive sessions

Subject: Post-incident summary: 2028-04-01 FastShop interactive streaming stalls (root cause & next steps)

Hi Diane / FastShop team — thank you again for the quick data you sent. Below is a concise post-incident summary and our planned actions. We'll schedule a 30-min review call for next week but wanted to get this documented promptly.

What happened
- Between 14:05–14:28 PDT on 2028-04-01, a subset of interactive streaming requests from FastShop experienced elevated tail latency and occasional stalls (8–20s).

Root cause (summary) - A localized edge shard in us-west-2 encountered an atypical combination of high-concurrency short sessions and a small fraction of long-running token-heavy requests that increased per-request scheduling and KV cache churn. This produced head-of-line stalls for many small interactive sessions.

Immediate mitigations we applied
- Applied a per-tenant routing override to route FastShop traffic away from the overloaded shard.
- Scaled edge worker pool in us-west-2 + increased batching thresholds for affected queues.
- Set per_tenant_max_concurrent_streams=3 and enabled aggressive prefix caching for FastShop to reduce scheduling pressure.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommended
- Temporarily switch critical flows to poll-based fetch (1s) for immediate resilience.
- Enable 1 retry with backoff on the client so transient stalls don't surface to end users.

Follow-ups & timeline
- Short (2–7 days): SRE will monitor telemetry and keep routing override in place while we validate stability.
- Medium (2–4 weeks): Implement per-customer routing policy so high-throughput tenants are isolated from small, latency-sensitive sessions.
- Long (1–3 months): Improve scheduling heuristics to avoid KV cache thrashing from mixed long/short session workloads; add automated surge classifiers.

Compensation
- We've opened HS-89321 in HubSpot to record impact; FastShop will receive a service credit proportional to the affected request volume. I'll coordinate with finance and your account team.

Attachments & links
- Postmortem draft (attached) and shared doc: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/fastshop-postmortem-20280401
- Jira ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4521

Next steps
- Propose a 30-minute call Wed 2028-04-04 15:00 PDT to walk through the postmortem and any configuration questions. If that doesn't work, please propose an alternate time.

If you'd like, we can keep the routing override up until after the call while you run an end-to-end smoke test.

Thanks for the partnership here — we'll follow through on the timeline above and share an updated postmortem with action owners.
